claims.text: The initial FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase FCC crystal.
The initial alloy has a random solute distribution.
The initial crystal has no pre-existing vacancy clusters or twin boundaries.
Yield-strength insensitivity over 10^8–10^10 s^-1 arises from nucleation of Shockley partials at solute-induced local lattice distortions rather than at vacancy clusters.
Differences in constituent atomic lattice parameters produce local resistance affecting partial-dislocation behavior in an HEA.
Solute-induced local lattice distortions act as nucleation sites for Shockley partial dislocations.
Shockley partial dislocations generate intrinsic stacking faults with HCP-like local stacking.
Yielding is initiated by thermal activation of Shockley partials from solute clusters having reduced local critical resolved shear stress.
The lack of strain-rate sensitivity is caused by athermal nucleation barriers dominating at the simulated high strain rates.
Orientation dependence of yielding is dictated by the Schmid factor of the active slip system.
Loading along <11-1> produces a higher maximum yield stress than loading along <110>.
The higher yield stress for <11-1> results from a lower resolved-shear-stress factor on the primary {111}<112> slip system.
HCP-like regions will revert to FCC stacking upon unloading.
An unchanged local coordination number of 12 distinguishes stacking faults from a true HCP phase transformation.
Yield strength is insensitive to strain rate but sensitive to temperature within the stated simulation regime.
Deformation is mediated by partial dislocations without twinning or phase transformation.
Local chemical short-range order may alter the magnitude of the orientation effect.

contradictions.description: Nucleation is described as thermally activated in one statement but as governed by dominant athermal nucleation barriers in another, without explaining how these descriptions coexist.

The predicted outcome correctly notes that both FCC and HCP environments have CN=12, but the falsification rule describes the coordination number as 'dropping to 12.' Thus CN=12 alone cannot discriminate HCP from FCC or a stacking fault.

The initial state definitively excludes pre-existing vacancy clusters, while the uncertainty statement says vacancy distributions have not been directly observed and the vacancy-cluster alternative remains unresolved.
